metric: validation_auroc is the fixed evaluator's AUROC. Higher is better. The x-axis is experiment number within a session.

sessions.conclusion: This modeling session substantially improved TCR-peptide-HLA binding prediction by replacing a basic mean-pooled embedding baseline with separate multi-kernel Conv1D sequence encoders and an interaction MLP, followed by residue-level cross-attention across split TCRalpha/TCRbeta, peptide, and HLA representations. Validation AUROC was further elevated by incorporating frozen BLOSUM62 and physicochemical amino acid features, adding dilated residual convolutions with Squeeze-and-Excitation gating, and training with label-smoothed MSE loss and exponential moving average (EMA) weight averaging. In the later stages, refining 13-term sequence interactions via a SwiGLU residual block with a skip connection, extracting mask-normalized attractive-repulsive residue affinities, and applying a depthwise-separable 2D convolution with top-8 hotspot pooling over pairwise affinity matrices drove the final performance gains. Overall, these cumulative architectural and training enhancements raised the validation AUROC to a best of 0.8230, with a corresponding AUPRC of 0.8093.

experiments.hypothesis: Replacing unnormalized dot-product projections in PairwiseAffinity with L2-normalized per-head cosine similarity scaled by a learnable per-head temperature will prevent seen peptides from inflating projection norms to saturate tanh affinities, improving unseen-peptide calibration and AUROC while preserving 0076's low validation MSE (0.1751) and high peptide-macro AUROC (0.8043).

sessions.conclusion: This autonomous modeling session established a baseline using binary cross-entropy loss and then substantially improved validation AUROC by replacing masked mean pooling with masked max pooling over the convolutional activations. Subsequent gains were achieved by introducing separate amino-acid embeddings for the peptide, HLA, and TCR chains, and progressively deepening the encoder to three masked convolutional blocks with ReLU activations. Finally, calibrating the pre-sigmoid logits with both learnable and fixed temperature scaling—specifically refining the fixed temperature to 1.75—yielded further improvements. Across the session, the model achieved a best validation AUROC of 0.7777 and a peak AUPRC of 0.7426.

sessions.conclusion: During this autonomous modeling session, validation AUROC was initially raised by introducing a 1D CNN over the embedded sequences, replacing mean pooling with global max pooling and negative padding masking. Performance improved further by widening the architecture—increasing the embedding dimension from 64 to 128 and the convolutional filters from 128 to 256. Finally, stacking a second Conv1D layer with 256 filters and a kernel size of 5 prior to pooling yielded the strongest model. This progression ultimately achieved a best validation AUROC of 0.7794 and an AUPRC of 0.7418.
